R1.rule: Before other work, scan the MEMORY.md index file in the memory directory.

R2.rule: After fixing a non-obvious bug (one whose surprise came from invisible behavior rather than a visible syntax error), record it as a memory entry.

R3.rule: When adding a memory entry, create a feedback_<short-slug>.md file in the memory directory containing the rule, its Why, and its How to apply.

R4.rule: When adding a memory entry, add a one-line pointer to it at the bottom of MEMORY.md.

R5.rule: After adding a memory entry, commit and push the change.

R6.rule: Keep each memory entry terse, no longer than one screen.

R7.rule: When editing a shared memory file, also update your personal copy of it, and when editing a personal copy, also update the shared copy.

R8.rule: Never instruct the user to select all and reindex on the Index Management page, because the row checkboxes are hidden and the mass action won't work.

R9.rule: When a feature needs a flat reindex or cache flush, implement a dedicated POST controller action to perform it rather than relying on mass actions.

R10.rule: Surface the reindex or cache flush action as a button on the admin page where the feature lives, and do not direct the user to Index Management.

R11.rule: When localhost or the live site returns HTTP 500 on all routes, check first whether Apache mod_headers is loaded.

R12.rule: If the logs show "Invalid command 'Header'", re-enable the missing Apache modules by running `docker exec ai-mms-web-1 a2enmod headers expires brotli rewrite deflate && docker exec ai-mms-web-1 apachectl -k graceful`.

R13.rule: Ensure `docker/entrypoint.sh` still contains the `a2enmod headers expires brotli rewrite deflate` line before the migration block.

R14.rule: When diagnosing a site 500 error, run the diagnostic checklist steps in the specified order.

R15.rule: When diagnosing a site 500 error, first confirm the 500 status with `curl -sS -o /tmp/h.html -w "HTTP=%{http_code}\n" -L http://localhost:8080/`.

R16.rule: When diagnosing a site 500 error, check `docker logs --tail 30 ai-mms-web-1` for the message "Invalid command 'Header'".

R17.rule: Only look at `var/report/` for Magento-level fatals after ruling out the missing mod_headers cause.

R18.rule: When writing a multi-line string value in a migration .sql file, never let any line inside the value end with a semicolon, because migrations/apply.php would split the statement there.

R19.rule: When generating data migrations with multi-line text values, end each value line with a tag (`>`) or a quote (`'`), never with a bare semicolon.

R20.rule: Before applying a migration, run `grep -nE ';\s*$' migrations/NNN.sql` and confirm every hit is a real statement terminator.

R21.rule: Guard content-rewrite UPDATE statements in migrations with a `MD5(value) = '<oldhash>'` condition so they are idempotent and skip rows edited after the migration was generated.

R22.rule: When local and remote databases diverge in this project, always write a SQL migration script to bring them into line.

R23.rule: Never propose dump-and-restore, direct replication, or other whole-database sync methods to reconcile local and remote databases in this project.

R24.rule: When the user reports local/remote DB drift or asks to "sync" databases, skip straight to drafting the migration SQL.

R25.rule: Before drafting a DB sync migration, ask the user what the target state should be (which fields/rows differ and which side is canonical).

R26.rule: Write the DB migration script as idempotent and limited to applying only the agreed changes.

R27.rule: Place production-bound DB migration scripts under `migrations/`.

R28.rule: Place local-only DB fixup scripts under `scripts/local-dev/`.

R29.rule: When asked to add, remove, or modify a field that admins see on the "Edit Course" page, do not treat an EAV migration alone as sufficient.

R30.rule:
When adding a field to the "Edit Course" page, add a `
…
` to the appropriate `dcf-tab-panel` in `dashboard/index.phtml`.

R31.rule: When determining where to place a new field in `dashboard/index.phtml`, search for nearby fields such as `name="training_hours"` or `name="course_type_select"` to find the right tab.

R32.rule: When adding a field to the "Edit Course" page, add a corresponding `if (($v = $req->getParam('<field>')) !== null) $product->setData('<field>', …)` line in `saveAction()` of `CoursesaveController.php`.

R33.rule: When adding a multiselect EAV product attribute on catalog_product, set source_model='eav/entity_attribute_source_table' on the eav_attribute row.

R34.rule: Any new multiselect (or select with admin-managed options) EAV migration in this repo must include backend_model='eav/entity_attribute_backend_array' and source_model='eav/entity_attribute_source_table' in the INSERT INTO eav_attribute statement.

R35.rule: When the values are also storefront-filterable, consider the tag-based path (see funding-badges-via-tags) instead of creating an EAV attribute.

R36.rule: After a bulk catalog attribute write, always reindex catalog_product_flat (including every per-store flat table catalog_product_flat_<store_id>).

R37.rule: After a bulk catalog attribute write, flush the block_html, full_page, and collections caches.

R38.rule: When verifying locally with curl, never send a Host header of tertiarycourses.com.<tld> against localhost.

R39.rule: When verifying a storefront page locally with curl, request http://localhost:8080/<url-key>.html directly.

R40.rule: To verify a specific store view locally, set MAGE_RUN_CODE via query string or environment variable, never via the Host header.

R41.rule: Before running a bulk attribute write, scan for existing per-store overrides on that attribute and either merge them or document why they are being clobbered.

R42.rule: Do not rely on setStoreId(0)->saveAttribute() to write at admin scope; prefer the direct SQL write at store_id=0.

R43.rule: For bulk catalog migrations that should affect every country, do not rely on saveAttribute() from a CLI default app context.

R44.rule: When saving a product attribute from a controller in this codebase, call updateProduct on the catalog/product_flat_indexer resource singleton for the product ID and each store.

R45.rule: After reindexing a single product's flat catalog entries, call Mage::app()->cleanCache with the catalog_product_<id> tag for that product.

R46.rule: For batch attribute operations, prefer a single reindexEverything() call on the catalog_product_flat index process at the end rather than per-product reindexing.

R47.rule: For batch attribute operations, flush the block_html cache type after the reindex.

R48.rule: For batch attribute operations, flush the full_page cache type after the reindex.

R49.rule: For batch attribute operations, flush the collections cache type after the reindex.

R50.rule: In SQL migrations under migrations/*.sql, reindex the flat catalog by running direct UPDATEs from catalog_product_entity_<type> into each catalog_product_flat_<store_id> table, since no PHP hook runs during deploy.

R51.rule: At the end of a SQL migration under migrations/*.sql, truncate the core_cache_tag table to force block_html and full-page cache regeneration.

R52.rule: When adding a new funding badge, append its name to getAllBadges() in Helper/Data.php.

R53.rule: When adding a new funding badge, add a course-badge--<key> CSS class for it in skin/frontend/ultimo/default/css/custom.css.

R54.rule: When adding a new funding badge, add a row for it to the getBadgeCssClass() map.

R55.rule: When adding a new funding badge, seed a tag row for it via a new migration.

R56.rule: Never add a column to the EAV (product attribute tables) for funding badges.

R57.rule: When asked where funding badges come from, answer that they come from tag_relation, not from a product attribute.

R58.rule: After any direct database tag write, reindex catalog_product_flat.

R59.rule: After any direct database tag write, flush the block_html and FPC caches.

R60.rule: When a migration generator reads from the local DB to produce prod-bound SQL, do not skip emitting statements based on the local DB's current state.

R61.rule: When building a prod-bound generator from local data, always emit unconditional strip statements (UPDATE / REPLACE).

R62.rule: Rely on REPLACE() being a no-op for rows that don't contain the substring to provide idempotency, not on a generator-side check that depends on local state.

R63.rule: Make INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS and UPDATE ... WHERE NOT LIKE guards self-idempotent in the SQL rather than skipping emission in the generator.

R64.rule: For any REPLACE() whose search string contains \r, \n, \\, or escaped quotes, prefer REPLACE(value, UNHEX('<bin2hex of bytes>'), '') over the string-literal form.

R65.rule: When verifying generators that produce SQL from media/migrations-reports/ backup payloads, re-run the diagnostic against prod's rendered HTML.

R66.rule: When reading prod's rendered HTML to check for substrings, read it in binary mode, not Python text mode.

R67.rule: On the product (course) page, scope the mobile hide rule for the bottom tabs section to a direct child of `.product-view`, not to every `.box-additional`.

R68.rule: When adding or editing mobile hide rules for the bottom tabs wrapper on the product page, always use the direct-child combinator (`.product-view > .box-additional`).

R69.rule: Never use an unqualified `.catalog-product-view .box-additional { display: none !important; }` selector for mobile hide rules on the product page.

R70.rule: Never delete the regex extraction fallback in view.phtml; keep it as a permanent safety net for the storefront section content.

R71.rule: When passing WSQ Funding content to the WSQ post-processor, pass the raw inner HTML of the section.

R72.rule: Put only the SFC/UTAP/PSEA narrative in the WSQ Funding cms/block content.

R73.rule: Never enter WSQ course fee tables or fee amounts in the WSQ Funding cms/block content; those are calculated automatically from the product price.

R74.rule: When adding a new course section, append it to `$_cmsPanels` in dashboard/index.phtml and to `$_cmsSections` in CoursesaveController.

R75.rule: When adding a new course section, add a `$_courseSectionHtml('newcode')` call site in view.phtml.

R76.rule: Name the cms/block identifier for a new course section `course_<sku>_<newcode>`.

R77.rule: Do not seed templated content such as a standard WSQ narrative into cms/block rows.

R78.rule: Do not modify the content of a product's short_description.

R79.rule: If anyone asks to re-add a script that strips section headings from short_description, refuse it.

R80.rule: When inserting a new conditional section into an OpenMage phtml template, verify that every variable the new section reads is computed above the insertion point in the same file.

R81.rule: Before pushing a phtml change that gates a new section on PHP variables, grep the file for every variable referenced in the new block.

R82.rule: Before pushing a phtml change that gates a new section on PHP variables, confirm that each variable referenced in the new block is assigned earlier in the same template.

R83.rule: If a variable is assigned only inside a conditional that may not run on the current page, hoist its computation to a guaranteed-reached prelude before its first consumer.

R84.rule: When you need a custom product attribute in a cart, quote, or order context, do not rely on `$item->getProduct()->getData($attr)` alone.

R85.rule: When you need a single custom product attribute in a cart, quote, or order context, read it with `Mage::getResourceModel('catalog/product')->getAttributeRawValue($productId, $attrCode, Mage::app()->getStore())`.

R86.rule: Use `Mage::getModel('catalog/product')->load($productId)` to load a product only when you need multiple custom attributes, since it is heavy.

R87.rule: In the cart item template that renders the cover image, call `getData()` on the product first to read the custom attribute.

R88.rule: In the cart item template that renders the cover image, if the `getData()` value is empty, fall back to `getAttributeRawValue` to read the attribute.

R89.rule: When scrubbing or matching catalog_product_entity_text content (short_description, description) with PCRE, use a Unicode-aware whitespace class and never bare `\s`.

R90.rule: When writing PCRE against EAV text columns, define a whitespace token like `$WS = '(?:\s| |\x{00A0}|\x{2007}|\x{202F})';`.

R91.rule: Use the whitespace token together with the `/u` modifier in every place where you would normally write `\s*` or `\s+`.

R92.rule: When the section name in a title alternative may have been pasted with Unicode dashes or curly quotes, widen the title alternative to match them.

R93.rule: After running a scrubbing regex, verify by re-querying for the literal marker text.

R94.rule: If any row still contains the section header markup after running the regex, suspect another invisible codepoint and hex-dump the offending region.

R95.rule: To make a custom email template manageable in the admin Transactional Emails grid, do not rely solely on registering a file template in config.xml; also seed a core_email_template database row.

R96.rule: When adding a transactional email the client must be able to edit, ship a file default at app/locale/en_US/template/email/<module>/<name>.html with @subject and @vars headers and register it in config.xml under <global><template><email>.

R97.rule: Seed the core_email_template row in a migration, with template_text set to the file body with the @subject and @vars comment blocks stripped, template_type set to 2 for HTML, and orig_template_code set to the registered file code.

R98.rule: In the same migration as the template seed, store the seeded row's template_id in a core_config_data config path (e.g. <module>/<feature>/email_template), so the sender reads it and edits to the DB row take effect.

R99.rule: When calling sendTransactional, pass a numeric template id to load the DB row, and keep the string template code as the ?: fallback that loads the file default.

R100.rule: When writing migration SQL with an inline HTML blob, ensure no line of the HTML ends with a semicolon, because the runner splits statements on lines ending in semicolons.

R101.rule: When writing migration SQL string literals containing single quotes, escape each single quote as two single quotes.

R102.rule: Before changing the clear rule on `.product-view > .box-additional`, check which column is currently tallest on a representative product page.

R103.rule: If the right secondary column is the tallest on the product page, set `clear: none` on `.product-view > .box-additional` so the tabs rise beside it.

R104.rule: If the left/image column is the tallest on the product page, set `clear: both` on `.product-view > .box-additional`.

R105.rule: Do not add a `clear` property to the inner columns (the `.grid12-4` img, primary, and secondary floats), because they must remain floated for the three-column layout.

R106.rule: When injecting JS that selects rows in a Magento admin grid, select a row by calling `checkbox.click()` on its checkbox.

R107.rule: Before calling `checkbox.click()` to select a Magento admin grid row checkbox, first check that `!checkbox.checked && !checkbox.disabled` holds.

R108.rule: Never select a Magento admin grid row by setting `checkbox.checked = true`.

R109.rule: To unselect a Magento admin grid row that is currently checked, call `.click()` on its checkbox.

R110.rule: When custom admin JS needs to programmatically tick grid checkboxes (per-row action injections, select-all toggles, delete-all buttons), use `.click()` on the checkboxes.

R111.rule: Apply the click-based checkbox selection rule to any future grid-automation JS.

R112.rule: When editing the Contact Us form, keep the field names name, email, company, telephone, courses, course_code, and comment unchanged, because the "Tertiary Courses Contact Form" email template resolves variables from them.

R113.rule: To confirm which contact form template is live, request /contacts/ with curl and grep the response for a distinctive class such as tc-submit.

R1.rule: When discovering an undocumented API, probe real endpoints using bogus credentials, not the user's account.

R2.rule: When probing a GraphQL API, probe candidate field names with bogus-credential requests, since GraphQL APIs often validate before authenticating.

R3.rule: When probing a GraphQL API, batch many candidate field names in one request using aliases.

R4.rule: When the schema of an API is unknown, decode responses leniently.

R5.rule: When the schema of an API is unknown, surface the service's own error message verbatim to the user.

R6.rule: When the schema of an API is unknown, ask the user to paste the service's error after their first real test.

R7.rule: After rebuilding the app, add a `?v=N` cache-busting query parameter to the URL when loading it in the in-app browser pane, incrementing N each time.

R8.rule: When filtering CeX results to games, select entries where superCatId == 1.

R9.rule: Make one CeX lookup per user scan, and never crawl CeX.

R10.rule: For CeX barcode lookups, keep only the product name and platform from the response.

R11.rule: Never store or display CeX product images.

R12.rule: Only fetch and store CeX prices under the conditions in the price rules.

R13.rule: If CeX requests get a Cloudflare challenge, fail with a clear error message.

R14.rule: Never work around a Cloudflare challenge from CeX.

R15.rule: Store CeX prices only for the user's own copies.

R16.rule: Query CeX prices once per copy, on that copy's own random date 20–40 days out, or when the user presses the "Update price" button.

R17.rule: Do not fetch or store CeX images when querying prices.

R18.rule: Never work around the Cloudflare challenge blocking CeX search (/v3/boxes?q=).

R19.rule: Do not price copies that have no barcode via CeX.

R20.rule: Give cookie and storage captures a readiness condition (`when`) so anonymous values are not captured before sign-in.

R21.rule: List every host outside the opened one and have the user confirm it.

R22.rule: Enable a Game Vault address only from the extension popup, never from a web page, because pages cannot trigger permission prompts.

R23.rule: Have the bridge ping the MV3 service worker every 20 seconds to keep it alive, since a port alone does not.

R24.rule: Do not give redirect recipes a `when` condition.

R25.rule: Never offer "Remember" for plain-http network addresses.

R26.rule: Run real-store checks for Humble and Steam on a config copy, and run checks for other stores only on a main server.

R27.rule: Call OwnershipService/CheckOwnership only from the background script.

R28.rule: Send at most 200 items per OwnershipService/CheckOwnership request.

R29.rule: Give every bundle game a mark, leaving it empty when the game is not owned.

R30.rule: Render store labels and marks inside closed shadow roots, with the same size, focus and events whatever the ownership answer.

R31.rule: Never show an unavailable ownership result as "not owned".

R32.rule: Do not check Fanatical's selectors automatically; only the user checks them.

R33.rule: Make Fanatical labels read only the page the user is viewing and store nothing.

R34.rule: Limit token storage to trusted contexts where the browser supports them.

R35.rule: Use one content script per allowed store, registered dynamically.

R36.rule: Save the store-page option whole from the popup's shown state (shownOwnership), never by read-then-write.

R37.rule: In Firefox, put no await before permissions.request(): start the write, then the request, with no await between them.

R38.rule: Treat a permission request that throws as not granted and turn the option back off.

R39.rule: On each store-script sync, inject into open store tabs that are not yet running the scripts, probing `__gvOwnershipStarted` first.

R40.rule: Make label.js ignore a second load.

R41.rule: Make orphaned content scripts stop, checking with alive().

R42.rule: Never treat store sites as Game Vault addresses.

R43.rule: Refuse store sites as Game Vault addresses in enableOrigin, originAllowed, activeSettings and the popup offer.

R44.rule: Add each new store or sign-in domain to extension/lib/storesites.js.

R45.rule: Enable developer mode via developerPrivate.updateProfileConfiguration before reloading the extension in end-to-end tests.

R46.rule: Load the unpacked extension in branded Chrome 137+ with Extensions.loadUnpacked over --remote-debugging-pipe and --enable-unsafe-extension-debugging, not --load-extension.

R47.rule: Under Xvfb, accept the permission prompt with `xdotool key Tab Return`.

R48.rule: Use happy-dom from web/node_modules for the extension's DOM tests.

R49.rule: Test the background in Node against a fake chrome object.

R50.rule: Write recipes as declarative data, never as code.

R51.rule: Do not use paid LLM services to recognize physical game boxes from photos.

R52.rule: A small local model may be used to recognize physical game boxes from photos.

R53.rule: When matching OCR text against a platform's title list, require the catalog title to be found inside the OCR text, not the reverse.

R54.rule: When fetching Wikipedia cover art that is non-free, include pilicense=any in the request.

R55.rule: Never commit photo files to the repository.

R56.rule: When resuming the cover-recognition spike, start from the "Before building it" list in its README.

R57.rule: Run OCR for cover recognition in the browser using ONNX.

R58.rule: Determine the game's platform from the banner text on the box or from the batch preset.

R59.rule: Perform fuzzy matching of recognized titles against the catalog in the Go server.

R61.rule: Have the user confirm the final game match before accepting it.

R62.rule: Keep the server pure Go, with no CGO and no ONNX runtime.

R63.rule: Never show rotating credentials (schema.FieldState settings) to the browser or accept them from the browser.

R64.rule: When a provider rotates a credential, write the new value into the settings map, and have the service persist it via Source.UpdateState.

R66.rule: Cache exchanged one-time codes in memory keyed by sha256(code) so that a Test followed by a Save reuses the same code.

R67.rule: Use internal/adapters/outbound/oauthsession for code-based OAuth sources (Epic, GOG, Xbox, Amazon and PlayStation).

R68.rule: Allow only one refresh at a time in oauthsession.

R69.rule: Always hand back the newest session in oauthsession.

R70.rule: Remember a spent refresh token together with its replacement for 8 days in oauthsession so the spent token is never sent again.

R71.rule: Use oauthapp for application tokens (client credentials).

R72.rule: Keep PlayStation's NPSSO in the settings and do not route it through sync.Preparer, since it is not a one-time code.

R73.rule: When Sony refuses the PlayStation refresh token, call Sessions.ForgetCode(npsso) in playstation.withToken.

R74.rule: After forgetting the code, sign in again with the NPSSO in playstation.withToken.

R75.rule: If a provider caches credentials in memory, always hand back the latest value on every call.

R77.rule: Never let two servers share a rotating credential.

R78.rule: Start test servers with the -no-unattended flag.

R79.rule: On a copied config, only scan Humble or Steam.

R80.rule: Never change the ExternalID format of an existing import, because a changed format duplicates copies on the next scan and brings back excluded items.

R81.rule: Never derive the keys for Battle.net, EA, or CSV items from game.MatchKey; use game.TitleIDKey, which is frozen.

R82.rule: Never rename a catalog system Name.

R83.rule: Never rename system names such as PC, the console names, or Other.

R84.rule: Never change the gameDoc, copyDoc, sourceDoc, or providerDoc field names in the adapter once they are released.

R85.rule: When changing the meaning of a stored field, bump the document's "v" version.

R86.rule: Each fixture in testdata/ must round-trip byte for byte.

R88.rule: An import must never clear a copy's CSV system override.

R89.rule: Cover providers must read store ids from the game's links, never from the copies' ids.

R90.rule: Each library source must also link the game to its store using the same id.

R91.rule: Define every platform, system, and link key as a constant in internal/domain/game/platforms.go.

R92.rule: Use the shared platform name strings across sources, such as "Steam" and "Epic Games".

R93.rule: PlayStation copies must use the platform names "PS4" or "PS5".

R94.rule: To drop a copy it imported earlier, a source must return that copy as Withdrawn.

R95.rule: Keep the EA source's Origin as "EA app" in lowercase, while its platform stays "EA App".

R96.rule: Every provider must map or exclude every system, as checked by game.CheckProviderCoverage.

R97.rule: Battle.net and EA items without a store id must get the key `<prefix>:` + game.TitleIDKey(title).

R98.rule: Version Game Vault releases with SemVer git tags, starting at v0.1.0.

R99.rule: Run `task docker:publish` only on a tagged, clean commit, since it publishes only those.

R100.rule: Run `task docker:publish` only when the user explicitly asks for it.

R101.rule: Run `task docker:publish` only after the user has run `docker login` themselves.

R102.rule: Never ask the user for, or handle, the Docker Hub token (DOCKERHUB_TOKEN).

R103.rule: Publish the dev image (`task docker:publish:dev` or `dev-image.yml`) only with the user's explicit go-ahead.

R104.rule: Publish version tags and `latest` only as part of a release, never as dev publishes.

R105.rule: Do not compile anything in the Docker image build; it only packages prebuilt output.

R106.rule: Keep applying the proxy and Host rules from the security-model when working with the trusted-networks setting.

R107.rule: Never scrape the EAN-Search public site, because its terms forbid automated queries and it has bot protection.

R108.rule: When getting data from EAN-Search, use only the paid API and never the public site.

R109.rule: When writing the consent wording for the Fanatical integration, make clear that the user accepts the risk, not the plugin's authors.

R110.rule: When listing game-data folders whose names contain brackets (such as `[id]`), use `os.ReadDir` instead of `filepath.Glob`.

R111.rule: Before writing or editing any Go code, load the write-go skill, every time.

R112.rule: Give every interface method a doc comment, including Descriptor().

R113.rule: Start member doc comments with the member's name (e.g. "// Forwarded reports that…"), never with the name followed by a colon.

R114.rule: Put each struct field on its own line in struct type declarations.

R115.rule: In struct literals with several keyed fields, put each field on its own line, even when the literal is short.

R116.rule: In struct type declarations, declare one name per field.

R117.rule: Do not apply the one-field-per-line rule to map literals, positional struct literals, or single-field struct literals.

R118.rule: Write constructors using the functional options pattern, not config or dependency DTO structs.

R119.rule: In constructors, pass required dependencies as positional parameters and optional ones as With… functional options with no-op defaults.

R120.rule: Write new Go code in the required shape from the start instead of relying on the lint auto-fix (task lint:fix).

R121.rule: Write missing interface doc comments by hand; the lint auto-fix does not add them.

R122.rule: When requesting embed.gog.com, do not follow HTTP redirects.

R123.rule: When writing test fixtures for Humble Bundle order data, copy the real API response shape instead of inventing values (for example, keyindex values).

R124.rule: If the first real IGDB sheet fails, ask the user for the warning text shown with the failure.

R125.rule: Never remove affiliate tags from ITAD data.

R126.rule: Never change prices from ITAD data.

R127.rule: You may add your own data alongside ITAD data.

R128.rule: You may use only part of ITAD data.

R129.rule: Do not use ITAD data for private non-personal use without ITAD's approval.

R130.rule: Never compete with ITAD or help a competitor of ITAD.

R131.rule: Do not build price alerts or a waitlist in Game Vault that compete with ITAD's.

R132.rule: Cache ITAD API responses rather than sending requests up to the rate limit.

R133.rule: Link to IsThereAnyDeal or credit its API when using its data.

R134.rule: Never probe the POST /lookup/shop/61/id/v1 endpoint with an empty array `[]`.

R135.rule: Ask the user for the result of the first real refresh before relying on the unverified sort order, flag meaning, or asset behavior.

R136.rule: When paginating the itch.io owned-keys endpoint, keep requesting pages until a page comes back empty; do not stop because a page is shorter than per_page.

R137.rule: When decoding any itch.io list value, accept either a JSON array or a JSON object, because empty lists may arrive as {}.

R138.rule: When describing the project's license, describe it as source-available and never call it "open source".

R139.rule: Keep the non-affiliation / trademark notice in the README.

R140.rule: If outside contributions are accepted, suggest a CLA so the user keeps the right to relicense.

R141.rule: When the browser loads a remote image, load it only through the `/media/proxy` endpoint, never directly from the remote host.

R142.rule: Route a remote image through `/media/proxy` only if its host is declared by a provider via `ImageHoster`.

R143.rule: Do not treat Spanish as a priority or special case in language-dependent features; the product is not Spanish-first.

R144.rule: For language-dependent features (metadata summaries, Wikipedia articles, provider requests), use the UI language and fall back to English when it is unavailable.

R145.rule: Take the language from the request or UI setting, support any language code, and fall back to English.

R146.rule: Write examples and docs in English, referring to "the UI language" rather than "Spanish".

R147.rule: Set the Priority header to `high` for attention and security events.
